AI Repository Standards

.github AI Customization Layout

A practical layout for repository-scoped AI assets: agents, skills, prompts, hooks, and instructions.

agents skills prompts hooks instructions
Workshop Repo: ai-workshop Use Left/Right arrows, Space, or buttons.

Conventional Structure

Recommended .github Layout

.github/ |-- agents/ |-- skills/ |-- prompts/ |-- hooks/ `-- instructions/

Not every repository needs every folder on day one, but this is the conventional layout to grow into.

Keep structure intentional and discoverable. Slide 2

Directory Roles

What Each Folder Is Responsible For

agents/

Specialized agent personas or modes for repeatable task types.

skills/

Operational playbooks with triggers, guardrails, and workflows.

prompts/

Reusable prompt templates for focused generation or analysis.

hooks/

Automation scripts for safety checks, policy, and logging.

instructions/

Repository rules that shape agent behavior and boundaries.

Five folders, five distinct responsibilities. Slide 3

agents/

Task-Specific Agent Modes

Defines reusable agent personas or modes for specialized tasks.

  • Typical naming: <task-name>.agent.md
  • Common contents: mission/scope, guardrails, expected outputs
  • Examples in this repo: python-review.agent.md, security-audit.agent.md
Goal: predictable behavior per task category. Slide 4

skills/

Workflow Playbooks

Contains domain workflows the agent can invoke for repeatable, multi-step tasks.

  • Typical layout: one folder per skill, each with SKILL.md
  • Path pattern: skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md
  • Include: triggers, use/non-use criteria, inputs, procedure, outputs
  • Example: skills/create-skeleton/SKILL.md
Goal: operational consistency and fewer ad-hoc runs. Slide 5

prompts/

Reusable Prompt Templates

Stores reusable prompt templates for focused analyses or generation tasks.

  • Typical naming: <task-name>.prompt.md
  • Common contents: role framing, task instructions, output checklist
  • Example: security-review.prompt.md
Goal: high-quality prompts with repeatable outcomes. Slide 6

hooks/

Policy and Safety Automation

Automation scripts and policies that run around agent workflows.

  • Typical layout: scripts under hooks/scripts/
  • Use cases: PII checks, policy enforcement, telemetry/logging
  • Examples: hook-logger.sh, pii-checker.sh
Goal: shift governance left without manual burden. Slide 7

instructions/

Repository Rules for Agent Behavior

  • Typical naming: *.instructions.md for scoped guidance
  • Broader guidance often lives in copilot-instructions.md or AGENTS.md
  • Common contents: coding conventions, architecture boundaries, test expectations, safety constraints

Current repo note: top-level AGENTS.md is the primary guidance source. Add .github/instructions/ when scoped instructions become necessary.

Goal: make behavior explicit, local, and auditable. Slide 8

Naming + Authoring

Conventions That Keep Things Maintainable

  • Use lowercase kebab-case names.
  • Prefer explicit task-oriented names (security-audit, create-skeleton).
  • Keep one concern per file.
  • Document trigger phrases and include do-not-use-when guidance.
  • Edit in place to version behavior; avoid duplicate variants unless experimental.
Simple conventions reduce drift over time. Slide 9

How It Works Together

Composable AI Workflow Architecture

  • instructions define repository rules and constraints.
  • agents define specialized modes.
  • skills define execution playbooks.
  • prompts define reusable task templates.
  • hooks enforce safety and policy before/after execution.

Together they provide consistent, auditable AI-assisted development workflows.
